subject: Re: Dedicated vs Private VPC - data isolation expectations / next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Liam Chen <liam.chen@finsecure.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Dedicated vs Private VPC - data isolation expectations

Hi Liam,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great to understand FinSecure's workload and the compliance constraints you're operating under. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying questions so we can scope the right deployment option (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private):

Summary from call:
- Primary requirement: customer ML workloads must not leave your VPC; audit logs and access to raw request/response data are restricted to FinSecure personnel.
- Secondary: KMS integration for key management and a SOC 2 / penetration test report are required before production.
- Traffic profile: ~200 rps peak, with spikes up to 350 rps for short windows; latency SLO target 250ms 95
- Timeline: aiming for pilot in Q3.

Questions to help us recommend the right path:
1) When you say "must not leave our VPC": is the requirement that inference process/data must run inside your VPC (on-prem or cloud VPC) rather than just encrypted at rest/in transit?
2) Do you have an internal requirement for customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS) vs customer-provided keys in Redwood-managed KMS?
3) Who is the right technical contact on your infra/security team for an architecture sync?

Initial recommendation based on today's call: it sounds like Private (VPC) or on-prem deployment is the likeliest fit because of the VPC constraint and KMS needs. Dedicated reserved capacity (Redwood-managed) would meet throughput and latency needs but would still route through our managed control plane and infrastructure — which may not satisfy the "no data leaves VPC" constraint.

I've attached a one-pager contrasting Dedicated vs Private for quick reference. Happy to set up a 30-minute technical call next week with Vivek (our infra lead) to go over architecture options and data flow diagrams.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm the single-sentence definition of "data must not leave VPC" (question 1 above).
- Introduce your infra/security engineer for a technical sync (question 3).
- We'll schedule a technical call (Vivek + Neha + your infra lead).

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment: redwood-dedicated-vs-private-one-pager.pdf
From: Liam Chen <liam.chen@finsecure.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@finsecure.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Dedicated vs Private VPC - data isolation expectations

Hi Marissa,

Appreciate the clear recap. Short answers below, hope this helps:

1) "Must not leave our VPC": we need inference to execute inside our AWS account VPC (preferably in private subnets). Persisted logs and request/response payloads must remain in our S3 buckets and be accessible only to FinSecure IAM principals. No PII or raw payloads may be stored in any third-party-managed service.

2) KMS: We need customer-managed keys (CMKs) in our AWS account; if Redwood can integrate with our KMS/HSM that works.

3) Tech lead: Priya Rao (cc'd) is our Sr. Cloud Security Engineer — she'll own the architecture sync.

Other notes:
- SOC 2 report: please provide copy; we also need pen test summary and third-party attestation.
- Network egress: must be controlled — minimal outbound connectivity; any control-plane calls must be auditable and documented.

Given that, it sounds like Redwood Private (VPC-hosted control plane or on-prem) is preferred. If Dedicated can be run in a bring-your-vpc model we could evaluate, but we expect to have strict review here.

Thanks,
Liam

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Dedicated vs Private VPC - data isolation expectations

Hi Priya / Liam,

Thanks for the clarity. That's very helpful. Quick responses and proposed plan: 

- CMKs: We support integrating with customer KMS for data at rest keys and can support HSM-backed keys when run in a Private/on-prem deployment. We'll capture exact key usage patterns in the architecture sync.
- Control plane: For Private deployments we can either: 1) run a customer-managed control plane inside your VPC (no control-plane traffic leaves your account) OR 2) run a hybrid model where control plane is in Redwood but data plane (inference) runs in your account — both options have tradeoffs and we'll document them for your security review.
- Documentation: attaching our SOC 2 Type II summary and pen test highlights (redwood-soc2-summary.pdf and redwood-pen-test-summary.pdf). If you need full reports we can provide under an NDA.

Proposed next steps:
1) Architecture sync: 30-45m with Vivek (infra lead) + Priya next Tue 6/16 @ 10am PT — does that work?
2) We'll prepare a short security appendix outlining data flow, control-plane calls, and KMS integration for your review before the sync.
3) If the appendix looks good we'll prepare a pilot SOW covering a Private VPC deployment and a 6-week pilot scope.

Please confirm availability for the 6/16 slot or propose alternatives.

Best,
Marissa

--

Hi Marissa,

6/16 10am PT works for me — thanks for scheduling. Looking forward to the security appendix ahead of the call. A couple of prep items from our side:
- Please include a brief diagram of the hybrid control/data plane network flows (we'll want to confirm no unexpected egress).
- Can you confirm whether logs/audit trails in Private mode can be pushed to our S3 with FinSecure IAM principals only?

If those are covered in the appendix we'll be in good shape to run the pilot SOW.

Priya Rao
Sr. Cloud Security Engineer, FinSecure
